inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 total revenue including £80.4m credit account interest (52 weeks to 26 April 2026, continuing operations, Coventry Arena restated out). FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:1106-1108.
inputs.share_count_basis: 432,499,241 basic = diluted weighted average FY2026 (dilutive potential shares under share schemes: nil, note 9, FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:2396-2398). Period-end count net of treasury is marginally lower after £18.1m of FY26 buybacks (~2.5m shares); the weighted figure is used as the documented, slightly conservative divisor. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings £1,651.3m (all non-current, incl. £94.3m Frasers Group Financial Services securitisation) less cash £388.9m = £1,262.4m, the company's own net debt figure (FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:906-907), balance sheet 26 April 2026 = latest filing. Lease liabilities (£878.6m) are EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). Known post-balance-sheet cash movements (Hugo Boss shares bought at EUR 38 to reach 47.89%, Sports Direct Malaysia sale proceeds) are carried as explicit equity_bridge items with their matching assets rather than folded into this anchor, so the anchor stays tied to the filing.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 net cash from operating activities £583.8m less gross capex £654.8m = -£71.0m (FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:1301-1312). Capex includes £397.1m of investment-property acquisitions, which is why the reported figure is negative; lease payments (£193.3m principal) sit in financing and are not in this figure. The engine projects from the component paths below, not from last_fcf; the identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is preserved for auditability.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income of £56.9m (mostly interest on equity-derivative deposits and cash) is NOT deducted: the company is a net borrower (net debt £1,262m), and finance income sits below operating profit so it never enters the EBITDA-based component build. Deducting it would double-charge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 segment reconciliation 'Share-based payments (4.5)' and cash flow 'Employee bonus scheme charge 4.5' (FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:2225, 2239). No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes KPI = 0 all years). FY24 £23.4m was the final charge of the FY2021 Executive Share Scheme; FY25 £0.8m, FY26 £4.5m.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchase of own shares £18.1m (financing, FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:1331); FY25 nil, FY24 £126.4m, FY23 £155.3m. SBC is tiny so the flat count is effectively already funded; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote GBp/share. No FX risk in the conversion; no dual listing to parity-check. Bridge marks: Hugo Boss at EUR 37.97 x EURGBP 0.8461, Accent at AUD 0.655 x AUDGBP 0.5273, Malaysia proceeds at USDGBP 0.7557 (all Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-10).
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 26 April (52/53 weeks ending last Sunday of April)
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free + 5.0% UK ERP x beta ~1.2 = ~10.5% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (SONIA + RCF margin, £3.3bn facility), 4.5% after 25% tax; market-value weights ~70% equity (£3.6bn cap) / 30% debt (£1.65bn borrowings ex-leases) = 8.7%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, governance (Ashley ~73% control) and the Hugo Boss exposure are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (FY26 principal £193.3m in financing + IFRS 16 lease interest £33.8m, FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:1326, 2349) = £227.1m = 4.26% of revenue is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (£878.6m) are excluded from net debt; D&A for the tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26 total £340.4m less ROU depreciation £133.1m = £207.3m = 3.9% of revenue, PPE note).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100%-consolidated; NCI book value £30.0m (FY26 balance sheet) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI profit share is immaterial (£1.2m FY26).
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: EBITDA driver is underlying post-IFRS-16 EBITDA before SBC: FY26 'Profit from trading' £1,005.9m less realised FX losses £24.8m = £981.1m = 18.4% of revenue (segment reconciliation FRAS.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:2222-2227). It therefore EXCLUDES the £249.9m of impairments inside reported operating profit (£216.7m International, mostly XXL/Twinsport/Holdsport goodwill; £15.9m UK Sports; £17.3m Premium Lifestyle), which are non-cash and non-recurring, and includes other operating income and the £14.8m investment-property fair-value gain. The CSV's EBITDA (operating profit + D&A = £726.7m) is post-impairment and is not the forward base. FY25 same basis ~£824m = 16.8%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating retailer: Sports Direct, Flannels, House of Fraser, Frasers Plus, International incl. XXL/Holdsport; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2, non-US + leases + non-operating assets). The strategic-investment programme is valued separately from the retail flows under the matching-asset rule: investment income (£281.8m FY26, mostly £223.2m option premiums received plus mark-to-market), investment costs, share of associates' profit and finance income are all below operating profit and are excluded from the flows, and their source assets -- Hugo Boss and Accent at today's market value, FVOCI long-term financial assets (ASOS, Mulberry, Boohoo and others) at fair value, other associates at book -- are added in the bridge, with the full derivative liability position (sold puts, CFDs, total-return swap, FX hedges, £366.9m) deducted and derivative assets (£53.6m) added. Investment property (£852.2m at FY26; £370m East Midlands/York outlets added July 2026) is NOT in the bridge: its rental income is inside Property-segment operating profit and its acquisitions are charged as capex (the FY27 capex path of 7% = ~£386m absorbs the £370m deal). HUGO BOSS STATUS (from FRAS.L_Analysis.json, 2026-10-10): the EUR 38.00 voluntary cash offer became unconditional after EU merger clearance; the additional acceptance period closed mid-August 2026 with Frasers at ~47.89% direct ownership and ~78% economic exposure including instruments; HB's boards recommended rejection and Frasers has declared the offer final. Frasers therefore does not (yet) control or consolidate Hugo Boss; the stake is carried at market as a non-operating asset with the post-year-end purchase cost shown as a matching deduction, and the retail-only three-scenario frame is retained. Consolidation of HB (~EUR 4bn revenue, lower margin, heavier leases) would require a rebuild of the flows. The Accent on-market offer at A$0.65 is unconditional; the stake is carried at the 22.9% FY26 holding because the post-year-end acceptance level is not disclosed in the sources. Price is the prior-session regular close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: medium-term revenue growth, anchored to FY2026 restated revenue
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (14-15%) exceeds revenue CAGR (-1.6% 3y / 8.7% 5y) by far more than 30%. Book value growth is inflated by FVOCI mark-to-market gains and retained investment income from the strategic-stakes programme and by the FY2021 COVID trough base; it does not describe the retail business's growth and is rejected as the growth source.
historical_growth.notes: 3-year CAGRs run FY2023 (53 weeks, restated for Game Spain and Coventry Arena discontinuations) to FY2026 (52 weeks); the 53rd week and the FY24-25 planned declines in Game UK, Studio Retail and wholesale depress the 3-year revenue figure by ~2pp. 5-year CAGRs run from the FY2021 COVID-closure trough and overstate trend. EPS 5y is null because FY2021 EPS was negative (-16.5p). Owner-FCF CAGRs are null because FY2026 owner FCF is negative (-£75.5m) on £397.1m of investment-property acquisitions inside capex; owner FCF FY20-FY25 was 53.2, 298.6, 288.4, 53.3, 391.6, 530.9 (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not deducted as the company is a net borrower). On the same reported basis the FY26 figure is distorted, not the trend; the component build normalises capex instead.

base.growth_note: FY27: ~1pp from annualising XXL (consolidated from 27 June 2025, so FY26 carried 10 months) plus ~145 planned international store openings and Frasers Plus book growth (£340m sales, 1.1m customers, 20.5% of UK online), offset by continued planned Game UK/wholesale/House of Fraser run-off, the Malaysia disposal and a soft UK consumer exiting FY26 with sector-wide excess inventory (management: pressures continuing 'into the start of FY27'). Decelerates to 2% nominal by year 7, consistent with ~2.7% UK sporting-goods market growth less legacy-estate attrition.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY26 underlying 18.4% (FY25 16.8%; gross margin 48.4% vs 42.9% FY23). Year 1 steps back 60bp for XXL integration losses, Nordic repositioning, ~£50m of UK NMW/NI cost inflation and the weaker H2 FY26 exit rate, then recovers to 18.5% as Elevation gross-margin gains, own-brand SKU rationalisation (70 -> 30 brands by FY28) and brand-partner mix mature. No credit for Hugo Boss/Accent consolidation.
base.capex_note: FY26 gross capex £654.8m = 12.3% of revenue, of which £397.1m was investment-property acquisitions; ex-property ~£258m = 4.8%. FY25 £411.7m (8.4%), FY24 £267.2m (5.0%). FY27 at 7% (~£386m) absorbs the £370m East Midlands/York outlet acquisition completed July 2026; property buying is assumed to continue at a declining pace and is charged as capex with no separate credit for the rental yield beyond what is in the margin path.
base.tax_note: UK statutory 25% plus overseas and disallowable leakage. FY26 cash tax paid £164.2m on ~£542m of underlying pre-IFRS-16 EBIT = 30% but included settlements; FY25 £140.3m on ~£480m = 29%. 26% is a modest normalisation toward statutory.
base.wc_note: Retailer with inventory £1,280m + receivables £979m (incl. the growing Frasers Plus credit book, target £600m balances) against payables £879m: growth consumes cash. 15% of the revenue change is drawn into working capital each year.

scenario_narratives.base: Elevation Strategy continues to lift gross margin and brand-partner access (Nike, adidas, Hugo Boss) in UK Sports and Premium Lifestyle, while International (~30% of revenue) absorbs XXL and Holdsport with losses narrowing over FY27-FY28 and ~145 new stores a year. Revenue grows 3-3.5% near term, decelerating to 2% nominal; underlying post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin dips to 17.8% in FY27 on integration drag, UK wage-cost inflation and a weak consumer exit rate, then recovers to 18.5%. Property acquisitions continue but taper from the FY26 peak; capex normalises to ~4.2% of revenue against 3.9% ex-lease D&A. The Hugo Boss stake (47.89% after the offer closed) is carried at market in the bridge with the EUR 38 purchase cost deducted and no earnings credit; Frasers neither controls nor consolidates HB in this case.
scenario_narratives.bull: Luxury 'green shoots' and brand-partner momentum convert Flannels and the Premium Lifestyle estate back to growth; the Nordics (XXL) and South Africa reach the 3-5 year plan targets (XXL back to profitability, Holdsport +10% EBITDA) and the 145-store international rollout compounds at 5-6% group revenue growth; Frasers Plus scales toward its £1bn sales / £600m balances / 2m customers targets with a >15% yield, and the Visa partnership adds fee income. EBITDA margin reaches 19.5% by FY31, capex falls toward 4%, and 8-20% property yields on the owned outlet estate are realised. Hugo Boss re-rates above the EUR 38 entry price, or Frasers gains control and the associate becomes an accretive consolidated business.
scenario_narratives.bear: UK consumer weakness and sector-wide excess inventory persist through FY27 (APBT already missed the £550-600m FY26 guidance); Game UK, House of Fraser and wholesale continue to shrink, International losses from XXL/Twinsport/Holdsport fail to narrow and further goodwill is written off, and brand partners' own DTC discounting compresses gross margin. Revenue is flat for two years and margin settles at 16%. Balance-sheet capacity is absorbed by the ~£520m already spent on Hugo Boss plus ~78% economic exposure via instruments: with the offer final and closed, HB's share price loses its EUR 38 support and a 20-30% fall costs £250-400m of bridge value; sold puts on ASOS/Boohoo/Mulberry are exercised at above-market strikes; leverage climbs toward 3x and capex and lease intensity stay elevated.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: the Board has withheld FY27 guidance, FY26 APBT missed the low end of guidance, ~£520m of debt-funded Hugo Boss purchases plus ~78% economic exposure sit on a share price that no longer has offer support, the FY26 exit rate was weak with sector-wide excess inventory, FY26 carried £250m of impairments on acquisitions less than a year old, and governance is controlled (Mike Ashley ~73% via MASH) with a history of opaque derivative positions. Bull cut to 25% because it requires a UK consumer recovery, an international turnaround in two newly acquired loss-making chains and a favourable Hugo Boss outcome to coincide. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Frasers is valued as a UK-led sports and premium-lifestyle retailer on the owner cash flows of the retail estate, with the strategic-stakes programme (Hugo Boss 47.89%, Accent, ASOS, Mulberry, Boohoo, derivatives) marked to market in the bridge rather than projected as earnings, and the post-year-end cash spent acquiring Hugo Boss shares deducted against it. Impairments, option premiums, mark-to-market gains and finance income are stripped from the flows; leases are charged in full as an operating cost (so lease liabilities are not debt); the share count is held flat with the small SBC charge expensed. The 14x terminal cap acknowledges a cyclical, discount-rated retailer that has rarely traded above ~6x EBITDA (the base case's implied terminal EV/EBITDA is ~5x), and the 15% hurdle entry price is built with its own terminal value at 15%. Broker targets span 750p (Shore, RBC) to 1,100p (Jefferies); the house weighted value sits inside that range.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hugo Boss: 47.89% owned at ~EUR 38 plus ~78% economic exposure via instruments, with the final offer closed and HB's boards having recommended rejection. The bridge carries the stake at market (EUR 37.97); a 20% fall in HB on the full economic exposure is roughly -£350m (-80p/share) and is not in any scenario's flows. Gaining control would instead require consolidating ~EUR 4bn of lower-margin, lease-heavy revenue -- a rebuild, not a driver tweak.

Derivative positions (sold puts, CFDs, total-return swap) on strategic stakes: fair value £366.9m liability at 26 April 2026; exercise at above-market strikes converts contingent exposure into cash outflow and FVOCI losses bypass the income statement.
UK consumer and sector inventory glut extending into FY27; no FY27 guidance from the Board; FY26 APBT missed guidance.
International acquisitions (XXL, Holdsport, Twinsport) taking longer to reach profitability -- £216.7m of goodwill was written off in FY26 within a year of acquisition.

Property acquisitions (£397m FY26, £370m July 2026) charged as capex: value depends on realised rental yields and the Property segment holding its margin; a further capex step-up without revenue would push base owner FCF below the modelled path.
Controlled governance (~73% Ashley via MASH Holdings, advisory role): related-party and capital-allocation decisions (stakes, property, no dividend) are made without a meaningful minority veto.
Interest-rate sensitivity: £1.65bn floating-rate bank debt (more after the HB purchases) plus £879m leases; each +100bp on WACC removes roughly 13% of the base equity value (1,061p -> 926p).
